name: Dudani Retail
lm_rationale: Finshore Management Services — 5 SME IPOs in 2026 (₹187.37 Cr), 80% positive listings, +3.76% avg listing-day gain (chittorgarh 2026 SME tracker).
net_proceeds: Of ₹9.26 Cr net proceeds, ₹3.97 Cr goes to working capital, ₹3.00 Cr to repay borrowings, ₹0.79 Cr to two computerised embroidery machines and ₹1.50 Cr to general corporate purposes; issue expenses are ₹1.29 Cr.
key_risks: One customer accounted for 37.37% of FY26 revenue and one supplier for 44.17% of purchases, while revenue slipped 2.73% and operating cash flow was negative in FY26 and FY25.
market_moat: Own women's-wear brand Divena plus licensed just-in-time manufacturing for fashion marketplaces and a quick-commerce supply arrangement, sold across Myntra, Amazon, Flipkart, Ajio, Nykaa Fashion, Tata Cliq and Snapdeal.
management: Promoters Akshay Dudani and Charu Dudani; 100.00% pre-issue promoter holding drops to 64.99% post-issue.
prose_business: Dudani Retail designs and makes women's ethnic and fusion wear (suit sets, kurtas, dresses, co-ords, sarees) under its Divena brand at a rented unit in Kartarpura Industrial Area, Jaipur, and trades men's wear as Millennial Men. It also makes licensed-label garments on a just-in-time basis for fashion marketplaces. Sales are almost entirely online through marketplaces and its own websites.
highlight_dev: The company is bringing embroidery in-house with two computerised multi-head embroidery machines (₹79.20 lakh, Baba Textile Machinery) to replace outsourced job work.
sector_outlook: The Prospectus (citing IBEF) projects India's textile and apparel market to reach US$350 billion by 2030.
peer_sentence: At 15.84x post-issue FY26 earnings, Dudani is cheaper than the two profitable peers in the Prospectus table, Nandani Creation (23.70x) and Purple United Sales (26.72x); Mish Designs is loss-making (−11.27x), which pulls the stated industry average down to 7.73x.
verdict_reason: 1.90x book and 15.84x P/E, but flat revenue and 37% one-customer exposure
why: Revenue has been flat for three years (₹25.13 Cr to ₹24.59 Cr), but EBITDA margin widened from 7.20% to 12.07% and PAT rose to ₹1.90 Cr. At ₹29 the price is 1.90x book and 15.84x post-issue earnings, below the profitable listed peers, and debt is low at 0.47x equity. Most of the money goes to working capital and a small embroidery capex, with ₹3.00 Cr repaying loans. The main risks are dependence on one marketplace customer (37.37% of sales), negative operating cash flow in the last two years, and a very small ₹10.54 Cr float. Finshore's 2026 listings were mostly positive but averaged only +3.76%, and Day-1 demand was 0.08x.
suggestion: Watch; valuation is modest but growth is absent, so apply only if subscription improves by close.
